title: Migrate legacy modem surfaces to a single shared implementation
description:
Migrate the current BPSK helpers, QPSK-only modulation code, and QPSK fading glue onto one shared modem implementation. This story is where the SOGRAND-era placeholder QPSK path is fully subsumed and the codebase is left with a single modem source of truth.

## Background

The crate currently has multiple modem entry points with overlapping responsibilities. Once the shared modem framework and simulation integration exist, those fragmented surfaces must stop owning independent functionality. The goal is not merely API compatibility; it is a single implementation path for modem behavior across the codebase. In this migration, duplicated modem code must be removed cleanly rather than deprecated.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `BpskAwgnChannel` and the existing QPSK and Rician surface are implemented through the shared modem framework rather than through bespoke modem implementations.
- [ ] The placeholder QPSK implementation no longer owns unique business logic that bypasses the common modem framework.
- [ ] There is a single modem source of truth for behavior and functionality; parallel custom modem implementations do not remain scattered across the codebase.
- [ ] Existing simulation tests and examples continue to work through the migrated surface.
- [ ] Obsolete duplicated modem logic is removed cleanly; deprecation shims are not introduced.

## Notes

This story should leave one coherent modem path in the codebase rather than parallel legacy implementations. Prefer direct deletion of superseded modem code once replacement paths are proven.
